title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: Cheon reduction with H-prime semiprime walks, sort-based matching, capacity and caps

claims.statement: Setting: BLS12-381 G1, generator P0 of prime order r, d=2^20 (6d divides r-1), input T=A_1=[s]P0 and A_i=[s^i]P0, i<=n, n>=2^20 (only T and A_d are read; the bound holds for every n>=2^20 including the scoring value 2^20), s uniform in 1..r-1. Claim: the deterministic classical attack of proof.md recovers s with success probability at least 0.40 using at most 2^116.8219 total target-group-operation equivalents (one equivalent = one batched incomplete affine G1 addition = 2000 AArch64 instructions, C=2000), including all preprocessing, failed runs, record routing, sorting, matching, caps, verification and output; preprocessing is at most 2^115.83 units and included; peak memory is at most 2^125.1 bytes (2^85 owner, 2^20 generating and 2^31 storage nodes, each counted at its full 2^40 bytes); no advice, no quantum step. Attack: Cheon's reduction to z=s^d in the order-m subgroup H of d-th powers (m=(r-1)/2^20). Baby and giant scalars are products a*w of two H-primes (primes q with q^m=1 mod r): w from the list W of the first 2^50 H-primes above 2^39, a from disjoint lists of H-primes in (2^77,2^97). Each chain advances by one batched incomplete affine G1 addition per step from a table of even multiples [g]Q, g<=2^33. The N=2^115.6644 baby and N giant points (6N^2/m=0.52) give 224-bit keys (bits 1..224 of the even one of y, p-y) invariant under the six GLV/negation automorphisms. The 2N records of 48 bytes are matched by 4 routing passes (19 instructions each), 3 local LSD passes (25 each) and one scan (10) on a shared-nothing cluster, nodes with 2^40 bytes of local RAM and no remote-memory instruction, block transfers charged as posting/polling instructions; per-record overhead is listed at 211 instructions (27 walk bookkeeping, 23 key, 4x19 routing, 3x25 sorting, 10 scan) and charged as 230. The run fails after 2^90 run-pair comparisons or 2^20 verifications (charged at the caps) or if an owner node would exceed C=2^33.32 records (mean 2^31.66, 3.15 times the mean, after reserving 2^36 bytes per node). The final d-th root uses 20 square roots and a 2^11-step search over the 2^20-th roots of unity. Hypotheses: (H1) the 6N^2 ratios x/(u x') are Poisson-like in H, so coverage is 1-exp(-0.52)=0.4055; (H2/H2') a fraction 1/2^20 of the primes near q are H-primes (density 1/(2^20 ln q) among integers), the 2^50-th H-prime above 2^39 is below 2^77 and consecutive listed H-primes differ by at most 2^33 (checked when W is built); (H3) the 154-bit key prefixes of the 2N records behave like independent uniform strings, giving cap-exceedance probability below 2^-11.6 each by Markov and node-overflow probability far below the budgeted 2^-20 (Chernoff), so success is at least 0.4055-2^-10.6-2^-20 and 0.40 is claimed. F_r multiplications in prime searches are priced at the measured 383 instructions of blst_fp_mul. Instruction counts are itemised, not measured on hardware; the bound is analytic, memory is exponential, toy experiments are evidence only at their stated scale; not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: mode all (the single initial run) runs ledger (exact recomputation of costs, caps, capacity, memory), coverage (scalar-level toy vs the Poisson model) and ec (Algorithm A end to end on toy j=0 curves with truncated keys, a false-match cap, d-th root and a node-occupancy test). Each mode can be rerun with more trials. Toy results are evidence at toy scale only.
